info.dots: Each dot is one observation. Colored dots are clear-day observations (one color per series). Gray dots are observations flagged as cloudy.

info.smooth: Smooth fits a Savitzky-Golay filter. If you leave cloudy points in, the filter pulls the smoothed line toward them - usually Remove cloudy + Smooth together is what you want.
info.showDots: Dots toggles whether the per-observation markers are drawn.

help.bands: RGB draws three bands as red, green and blue. For Sentinel-2, B04 B03 B02 is natural colour and B08 B04 B03 shows vegetation in red. Single band draws one band through a colormap. Index computes a value per pixel from bands, for example NDVI: (B08-B04)/(B08+B04).
help.range: The values stretched from darkest to brightest: pixels below Min are drawn black and above Max white. Sentinel-2 reflectance usually sits between 0 and 3000, and NDVI between -1 and 1. Narrow the range to bring out detail in dark or bright areas.
help.colormap: The colours a single band or index is drawn in, from Min to Max of the range. Viridis suits most continuous values; RdYlGn suits vegetation indices such as NDVI.
help.colour: Gamma brightens the mid-tones above 1 and darkens them below 1. Contrast steepens the change around the middle. Saturation makes colours stronger above 1 and greyer below 1. These sliders write the color formula, for example: gamma RGB 1.5 sigmoidal RGB 10 0.35 saturation 1.2.
help.advanced: Resampling decides how pixels blend when you zoom in: nearest keeps them sharp, bilinear smooths them. Nodata is the pixel value drawn as empty, for example 0. The color formula takes rio-color operations, for example: gamma RGB 3.2 saturation 0.8 sigmoidal RGB 25 0.35.
